title: Yum Emoji 😋 Meaning: Delicious Food and Cheeky Fun
description: 😋 licks its lips to say “yum.” It's the go-to emoji for tasty food, cravings, and hunger, with a playful and occasionally flirty side. See how it's used.
summary: The 😋 face savoring food, often called the yum emoji, smiles with its tongue poking out to one side as if licking its lips. It means something is delicious or the sender is hungry and looking forward to eating. It is also used for cheeky, playful teasing.
meaning: This is the emoji for good food. The tongue at the corner of the mouth is the cartoon gesture for “mmm,” and people attach 😋 to photos of dinner, restaurant recommendations, recipes, and announcements that something is in the oven. It can mean the meal was delicious or that it is about to be. “Tacos tonight 😋” is anticipation; “those tacos 😋” is a review.

Hunger and craving are close relatives. Someone might send it in answer to “what do you want to eat?” or alongside a picture of a dessert they cannot have. Food bloggers, home cooks, and restaurants use it constantly, and it is one of the few smileys whose literal meaning is still its main one.

Outside food, 😋 works as a lighthearted, slightly mischievous face. The stuck-out tongue and smiling eyes give it a “hehe” quality, good for teasing or being pleased with yourself: “got the last parking spot 😋.” In this sense it overlaps with the tongue-out faces, though it is milder and cuter than they are.

It can be flirtatious. Saying someone looks 😋 is calling them a snack, a use that follows naturally from the food meaning. This is common enough to be understood but depends heavily on context. Sent about a person's photo it implies attraction. Sent about lasagna it implies lasagna, and most uses are of the second kind.

contexts.label: In food posts and captions
contexts.body: Its home ground. It sits under pictures of brunch, baking, barbecue, and takeout, and in reviews and recipe shares. It signals appetite and approval in one character. Pairing it with the specific food emoji is typical, as is using it to tag a restaurant visit or holiday meal.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Shows up in everyday meal planning and when friends tempt each other with food photos. It is also a friendly, goofy sign-off after a joke. Because it looks happy and harmless, it softens teasing. People rarely misread it, which makes it a safe playful option.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Usually still about food, or simple playfulness. If it is a reply to your selfie or a comment on how you look, it is a flirtatious way of saying you look good. Suggesting dinner and getting 😋 back means they like the idea. Check what it refers to before assuming more.

examples.meaning: Eagerly looking forward to a favorite meal.
Admiring someone's cooking and wanting some.

examples.text: Beat you to the last donut 😋

examples.meaning: Flirty compliment calling the person attractive.

combos.meaning: Craving or enjoying pizza; swap in any food for the same effect.
Mouth watering, then satisfied; the food looks and tastes great.
Delicious and possibly spicy, or a flirty “looking hot.”

confusedWith.difference: 🤤 has drool running from its mouth and expresses intense desire, for food or for a person. It is wanting, sometimes exaggeratedly. 😋 is enjoyment and playful appetite, and comes across as cuter and less extreme.
😛 sticks its tongue straight out with open eyes. It is for teasing and silliness, not eating. 😋 has smiling eyes and a tongue curled to the side, which is what links it to tasting something good.
😜 winks with its tongue out and means “just kidding” or wild fun. It has no food association. 😋 can tease as well, but more gently, and its primary meaning remains “yum.”

avoid: Don't comment it on a stranger's or coworker's photo of themselves, where it reads as calling them tasty.
Avoid it in serious discussions of diet, illness, or food insecurity, where a lip-licking face is insensitive.
design: A yellow face with smiling, curved eyes and a closed-mouth grin, with a pink or red tongue sticking out at one corner. The tongue usually points up toward the cheek, as if licking the lips. Apple, Google, Samsung, and Microsoft all use this arrangement. Which side the tongue appears on differs between some designs, with no effect on meaning.

faqs.a: Occasionally. When it responds to a person's appearance, it suggests they look good enough to eat, which is flirtatious. Most of the time it is about actual food or light teasing, and no flirtation is intended.

faqs.q: What does 😋 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: Check the subject. About food, it means yum. After a joke, it means they are being playful. About you or your photo, it is a cheeky compliment. The meaning does not depend on the sender's gender.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😋 and 😛?
faqs.a: 😋 has smiling eyes and its tongue at the side, tied to tasting food. 😛 has open eyes and its tongue hanging straight out, tied to teasing. 😋 is the one to use for anything delicious.

faqs.q: Can I use 😋 for things other than food?
faqs.a: Yes. It works for playful satisfaction, small victories, and gentle teasing. Readers will follow easily. The food sense is the default, though, so in a message that mentions a meal it will always be read that way first.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😋 and 🤤?
faqs.a: 😋 means tasty or playfully pleased. 🤤 means craving something so much you are drooling. 🤤 is stronger and is used more often about attractive people, while 😋 stays mostly at the dinner table.
